reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing and replaying the record, returned to the 2026–2027 guide, the year roster and the separate project pages. Reconstructed the complete credit allocation and checked the 60 EC foundation gate, compulsory project progression and restricted elective inventory. Reconsidered the selected UCR workbook content for organization, quantitative methods and software as three distinct approaches and checked the revised alignment against the finished record. This is a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The 2026–2027 guide confirms the standard Dutch-taught, part-time Information Science BSc and its six learning lines. The 180 EC inventory consists of 55 EC of compulsory foundation courses, 65 EC of later compulsory taught courses (including the 10 EC methods course and 5 EC project preparation), 15 EC restricted choice, 30 EC free electives and a 15 EC final project. The six restricted choices are Python Programming, GIS, Analysing Big Data for Dynamic Systems, Innovation Management, Organizational Consulting and Coaching, and Open Innovation. The guide asks students to choose three across the list. The two groupings are themes rather than formal separate degrees or routes.

Both September and February model rosters place 5 EC of free space among the foundation courses, consistent with the 60 EC foundation threshold for the information science methods course. That threshold includes the academic skills course. The 5 EC foundation elective is within the 30 EC total. Communication Skills requires at least 30 foundation EC, Enterprise Modeling builds on Introduction to Information Science, and Ontology Engineering builds on logic. Software Engineering requires introductory computing, logic, object-oriented analysis and programming, and databases. Graduation Project Preparation follows the rest of the taught program and electives unless the examiner grants permission. It must be completed immediately before the 15 EC independent research project. The standard 10 EC methods course is shown once; the intensive option is an alternative delivery of the same requirement.

The first option integrates Python, SQL, data science and algorithms with accounting, product design, organizational behavior and digital strategy. Market inquiry, quantitative and qualitative methods and responsible technology support informed adoption. Accounting & Corporate Finance adds direct costing, budgeting and performance overlap, improving the organizational option more than a second general methods course. The second option shifts to a sustained quantitative spine with linear algebra, probability, numerical computation, linear systems, machine learning and neural networks. Research Methods & Statistics and experimental methods provide empirical grounding. The third option builds software, networks, operating systems and algorithms on programming, logic and mathematics and retains databases and technology ethics; its systems depth serves the documented programming and technology learning line. Database Management Systems substantively supports design, querying and authorization based on its description. Other description-only courses support strategy, user inquiry and reinforcement learning on their stated content. Privacy and social consequences are addressed through AI ethics and governance; OU offers more dedicated information security. Enterprise modeling, ontology, specialist project management and a required 15 EC project remain distinct gaps. UCR independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC. The three options exceed the 30 EC difference floor and have separate substantive aims.
